trial_name.text: Study 20020408 (ABX-EGF plus Best Supportive Care Versus Best Supportive Care)

citations.quote: Protocol 20020408-entitled “An Open-label, Randomized, Multi-center, Phase 3 Clinical Trial of ABX-EGF plus Best Supportive Care Versus Best Supportive Care in Subjects with Metastatic Colorectal Cancer” is the sole pivotal study.

Protocol 20020408-entitled “An Open-label, Randomized, Multi-center, Phase 3 Clinical Trial of ABX-EGF plus Best Supportive Care Versus Best Supportive Care in Subjects with Metastatic Colorectal Cancer” is the sole pivotal study.
The pivotal study (20020408), a phase 3 randomized, controlled, open-label study evaluating the efficacy and safety of panitumumab plus BSC versus BSC alone, enrolled 463 subjects at 81 non-US sites.

design.text: Open-label, multinational, randomized (1:1), controlled trial of panitumumab 6 mg/kg every 2 weeks plus best supportive care (BSC) versus BSC alone, stratified by ECOG performance status and geographic region.

citations.quote: Patients were randomized 1:1 to receive panitumumab at a dose of 6 mg/kg given once every 2 weeks plus best supportive care (BSC) (n = 231) or BSC alone (n = 232) until investigator-determined disease progression. Randomization was stratified based on ECOG performance status (0–1 vs. 2) and geographic region (Western Europe, eastern/central Europe, or other).

population.text: Patients with EGFR-expressing metastatic colorectal cancer who had disease progression during or after fluoropyrimidine-, irinotecan-, and oxaliplatin-containing chemotherapy.

citations.quote: Study 20020408 is a randomized phase 3 clinical study conducted in patients with refractory, metastatic colorectal cancer who had failed fluoropyrimidine- irinotecan- and oxaliplatin-containing regimen(s). There is no effective therapy for this patient population.

endpoint.text: Progression-free survival (PFS) was the primary efficacy endpoint.

citations.quote: Progression-free survival (PFS) is the primary efficacy endpoint.
A total of 463 subjects were randomized into this study (231 in the panitumumab plus BSC group and 232 subjects in the BSC alone group).

result.text: Statistically significant prolongation of PFS with panitumumab + BSC vs BSC alone (hazard ratio 0.544 [95% CI 0.445, 0.665]; stratified log-rank p < 0.0001); mean PFS 96 days vs 60 days. No improvement in overall survival was demonstrated.

target_moa.text: Panitumumab is a human IgG2 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds specifically to the human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) and competitively inhibits binding of EGFR ligands, preventing ligand-induced receptor autophosphorylation and activation, resulting in inhibition of cell growth and induction of apoptosis.

citations.quote: Vectibix™ (panitumumab) is a recombinant, human IgG2 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds specifically to the human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions include dermatologic toxicity (reported in 90% of patients; severe in 16%), fatigue (26% vs 15% BSC), abdominal pain (25% vs 17%), nausea (23% vs 16%), diarrhea (21% vs 11%), and hypomagnesemia. Most serious events include severe infusion reactions (~1%) and pulmonary fibrosis (<1%, 2/1467).

description.text: Added indication for Vectibix in combination with sotorasib for KRAS G12C-mutated mCRC after prior fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application adds a new indication of Vectibix, in combination with sotorasib, for the treatment of adult patients with KRAS G12C-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), as determined by an FDA approved test, who have received prior treatment with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy. It also adds the following statement to the Limitations of Use: "Vectibix is not indicated for the treatment of patients with RAS-mutant mCRC unless used in combination with sotorasib in KRAS G12C-mutated mCRC."
